01 / 01 / The problem

Too many poor-fit leads

A name is not enough.

A lead can still be the wrong person for your service.

Wrong service
They need something you do not provide.
Wrong area
They live outside the area you serve.
Missing information
You cannot judge whether they fit.

Problem framing supplied by Taylor Cunningham. Examples illustrate poor fit.

Source and presenter notes

Open with poor-quality leads, one of the two problems Taylor identified. These are illustrative failure modes, not measured industry prevalence or a claim about every lead supplier. Lead Gen Engine quality means matching the agreed brief and passing the documented checks.

02 / 01 / The problem

The same lead, shared

You are competing already.

When a lead is shared, several businesses can be chasing the same person.

Illustrative shared-lead model. No market-wide figures are claimed.

Source and presenter notes

Explain the second problem in ordinary language: a supplier sends the same lead to multiple buying businesses. The three branches are a teaching diagram, not an industry statistic. Do not claim all suppliers operate this way.

03 / 02 / Our offer

Better fit. Not shared.

Checked for your business.

Your service, your area and your agreed customer criteria.

Supplied to your business.

We do not share the leads we supply to you with other buyers.

Lead Gen Engine offer, confirmed by Taylor Cunningham. Quality is defined by the agreed brief and checks.

Source and presenter notes

Taylor confirmed the offer on 7 October 2026: high-quality leads that are not shared. Present non-sharing as our supply commitment, not proof that nobody else can independently identify or contact the same person. The walkthrough demonstrates selection and validation; it does not audit an exclusivity allocation system or claim guaranteed enquiries, appointments or sales.

21 / 06 / Checking every contact

Four clear outcomes

1

Already in the file?

Remove the exact repeat.

2

Fails a rule?

Leave it out of the delivery.

3

Something is unclear?

Set it aside for review.

4

Passes every check?

Keep it for the checked list.

Illustrative United Van Lines example. No affiliation or completed lead results claimed.

Source and presenter notes

Plain-English labels correspond to exact duplicates removed, excluded, held and accepted. Apply precedence in that order after evaluating all checks. Exact duplicate means all source values repeat, not merely a repeated person’s name or identifier. A measured failure takes precedence over unresolved evidence. This is not an appointment or consent check.

22 / 06 / Checking every contact

Unclear is not a pass

Example: Low interest
Leave it out. It fails the agreed Medium or High requirement.
Example: no usable interest rating
Set it aside. Resolve the missing evidence before accepting it.

Illustrative United Van Lines example. No affiliation or completed lead results claimed.

Source and presenter notes

These are illustrative rule paths, not actual United records. Low score is excluded. Unknown score is held if no measured failure exists. A missing signal cannot become a pass simply because the audience query requested Medium or High.

23 / 06 / Checking every contact

Every record is accounted for

Original file
KeptLeft outHeld for reviewExact repeats removed

The four outcome counts must add up to the number of rows we started with.

Illustrative United Van Lines example. No affiliation or completed lead results claimed.

Source and presenter notes

Accepted + excluded + held + exact duplicates removed = input rows. Count final outcomes once each. Do not add failed-check totals together, because one record can fail more than one check. Show only actual counts after an authorised rehearsal.
